name: wake-slider

frames.best_why: The handle is mid-drag with a clear raised wake of taller bars and the value at 86%.

tagline: Thin bars rise into a wake as you drag the volume across them.
summary: A horizontal volume control drawn as a row of slim vertical bars. Bars up to the value glow white, and dragging faster lifts the bars around the handle into a short wave that settles when you stop.
appearance: A dark rounded card holds a small title and subtitle above a single row of about thirty evenly spaced rounded bars. Filled bars are pale grey and the rest sit dim, with a percentage at the right.
behaviour: Clicking or dragging anywhere on the bar row sets the level, and the lit bars follow the pointer. Moving quickly lifts neighbouring bars into a peaked wake that flattens as the drag slows.
demo_content: Master volume, Studio Monitors · Output 1-2, values from 22% to 86%.
use_when: An audio, brightness or any 0-100 control wants a more tactile readout than a plain track and knob.
avoid_when: The wake only shows mid-drag, and on touch the narrow bars make precise values fiddly.
customise: Value, min, max, step, bar count, height, gaps, colours, sensitivity, wake reach and skew are props; the label format is a function prop.
weight_why: 32 CSS-transformed bars updated by springs only while the value moves.

a11y.note: A hidden slider button makes every key work and exposes value text, but it has no visible focus ring.

polish_why: Tactile, well-spaced bars and a clear wake; the unfilled bars nearly vanish on the card.
title: Wake Slider
